newsitem.title: PERU: Peru starts new talks with Marxist hostage-takers.
newsitem.headline: Peru starts new talks with Marxist hostage-takers.

text.p: Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo on Thursday began a fourth round of face-to-face talks with Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.

A white Red Cross car carried a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) spokesman, believed to be second-in-command Rolly Rojas, the short distance between the residence and a safe house across the street where the talks were being held.

Also present were the three members of a "guarantor" commission overseeing the talks -- Red Cross representative Michel Minnig, Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent, and Vatican representative Roman Catholic bishop Juan Luis Cipriani -- as well as Japanese government observer Terusuke Terada.
Palermo met Rojas for three rounds of talks last week that apparently brought nothing other than a commitment to meet again.

The MRTA took over the residence Dec. 17 and is holding its captives as bargaining chips in their demand for the release of some 400 jailed comrades. President Alberto Fujimori's government has flatly ruled this out.
Police tightened security around the residence as the talks started.
